answers.flag: Option A needs a stop and start, which is downtime, so a candidate who reads 'minimal downtime' strictly or who thinks of the daily peaks as a reason to scale out could defend C; the stem does not say how long a stop and start may take or whether a short maintenance window is acceptable.

case.label: C
case.text: An Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer is the standard answer for changing daily load and growth, and it avoids the stop and start of A. A candidate can argue that an Auto Scaling group with minimum, maximum and desired capacity of 1 still replaces a failed instance and that the policy is simply never needed. The stem also says 'minimal', not 'zero', downtime, but the stem states that the application cannot run as several copies and keeps its data on the instance's EBS volume, so a multi-instance group across two Availability Zones with scale-out breaks the application. C is therefore wrong, but it is the option a pattern-matching candidate picks, and the cue 'cannot run as several copies' is what gives the answer away.
